title: Enter keys get broader model access
summary:
Enter keys gained broader model access, Bearer authentication became easier to use, and generation responses gained consistent usage headers.

Valid Enter tokens now bypass tier checks for text models and Kontext. Kontext still has a 30-second queue interval and tier-based concurrency caps. The Pollen FAQ now explains that frontend and server-to-server keys can access free and paid models, with paid models spending Pollen.

Enter now reads API keys from `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, and its API docs let developers test requests with a Bearer token. Browser preflight support was added to the image and chat proxy routes. An authentication guide covers the existing access methods, while a new control lets those routes require a session for free-usage requests.

Image and text responses now use a shared set of model and token-usage headers when the data is available. Image responses report `x-model-used` and image-token counts; streaming text responses can send usage in HTTP trailers.

daily.title: More models with Enter keys
daily.text: Use a valid Enter token to access text models and Kontext without model-tier checks. Kontext still has queue and concurrency limits. [Browse models](https://enter.pollinations.ai/models).

daily.title: Bearer keys for generation
daily.text: Send an Enter API key in the `Authorization: Bearer <key>` header, or enter it in the interactive API docs to test authenticated requests. [Open the API docs](https://gen.pollinations.ai/docs).

daily.title: Usage in response headers
daily.text: Read model and token-usage details from image and text response headers when available. Streaming text responses can include usage in HTTP trailers. [Open the API docs](https://gen.pollinations.ai/docs).
